title: Ad of the Week #2: log the first three seconds in four fields
hook: Hook rate says an opening worked. It cannot say why.
caption:
Hook rate says an opening worked. It cannot say why.
The first three seconds can, if you write them down the same way every time.

Ad of the Week #2 is a method, shown on a made-up example: a festive gifting ad for a tea brand. No real brand and no real numbers.

I log four things about the opening of an ad. What is in the first frame. What the first words promise. Who is on screen. When the product shows up.

Same four fields, same order, every ad. After twenty ads you can sort the sheet and see which kind of opening your good ads share.

A quiet week is a good time to log this year's ads.

slides.headline: The first *three seconds*, written down
slides.sub: A logging method, shown on a made-up gifting ad.

slides.headline: Averages hide the *opening*
slides.body:
Hook rate tells you people stayed past the opening.

It cannot tell you what was in it. So two ads with the same hook rate teach you nothing about the next brief.

The fix is a log. Four fields, the same for every ad.

slides.headline: Four fields, *every ad*
items: First frame — what you see before anything moves
First words — the promise, spoken or on screen
Who — founder, creator, customer or nobody
Product in — the second it first appears

slides.headline: A festive *gifting ad* for a tea brand
slides.body:
First frame: hands tying a ribbon on a box.

First words: 'For the aunt who has everything.'

Who: a customer, at home.

Product in: second two, when the box opens.

slides.headline: What twenty logged ads *show you*
items: Sort by first frame — what your good ads share
Sort by product in — early or late, by cost per order
Read the blanks — openings you have never tried

slides.headline: Log the opening. *Then* read the average.
slides.sub: Four fields, twenty ads, one sheet.
